faqs.question: What does Ebenezer Tarubinga do?
faqs.answer: I build production AI systems: retrieval, agents and computer vision for city infrastructure, edge to cloud. I publish on the research side of the same problem, and I build the platform underneath a nine-product fleet.

faqs.question: What does his research cover?
faqs.answer: Four mechanisms for one problem: learning to label every pixel from a handful of examples, without letting the model's own mistakes compound. Two are peer-reviewed.

faqs.question: What is CW-BASS v2?
faqs.answer: A foundation-model teacher's confidence saturates, so a one-pass gate asks whether its confident set deserves the confidence it demands.

faqs.question: What is PixCon?
faqs.answer: A pixel memory that admits only labeled pixels, keeping contrastive positives free of pseudo-label noise, with nothing added at inference.

faqs.question: What code and checkpoints are released?
faqs.answer: Training code, configs and released checkpoints for all four papers.

faqs.question: What has he released as open source?
faqs.answer: hwpkit: Read, edit and extract text from Korean HWP and HWPX files in pure Python, with no Hancom Office and no Windows. tzohar-engine: A framework for personal and academic websites: typed section blocks, ORCID and BibTeX ingestion, and a licence that leaves the owner holding their own copy. claudehop: Move an agent CLI between accounts without logging in again. One file, standard library only.

faqs.question: What did he research at Korea University?
faqs.answer: Semi-supervised segmentation under Prof. Seong-Whan Lee (IEEE Fellow): four first-author papers, ~10K lines of multi-GPU PyTorch training infrastructure, one Korean patent filing.

faqs.question: Is he open to new work?
faqs.answer: Open to ML and research-engineer roles, and to research collaborations.
